title: Off-peak Recapture Pricing Sensitivity Sheet
content:
Sheet overview: This workbook models the economics of actively recapturing off-peak hours and weekend slack in reserved GPU pools. Goal: quantify the unit cost delta and reserve commitment sizing improvement if we can reliably backfill off-peak capacity with burst customers and preemptible workloads.

TABS: Assumptions | Hourly Utilization | Backfill Rules | Price Sensitivity | Scenario Summary | Key Outputs & Actions

1) Assumptions (tab):
- Total reserved GPUs: 120 A100-equivalent units (expressed in vGPU-hours).
- Base committed monthly cost: $432,000 (provider invoice amortized).
- Baseline utilization profile: Weekday peak util 85% (9am-6pm), shoulder 55% (6am-9am, 6pm-11pm), overnight 18% (11pm-6am), weekend aggregate 28%.
- Off-peak window definition: weekdays 11pm-6am + full weekend (Fri 11pm–Mon 6am) -> ~40% of hours.
- Backfill capture rate: fraction of off-peak capacity we can monetize; baseline 40%, conservative 20%, optimistic 70%.
- Backfill unit revenue: $0.45 / GPU-hour (burst/spot price we can sell to third parties).
- Intrinsic marginal cost (electricity + infra ops) assigned: $0.06 / GPU-hour.
- Penalty for under-provisioning (lost conversions / SLA) expressed as expected revenue loss: $50k/mo if we under-allocate during peak (safety buffer).
- Preemptible mix discount: when we allow preemptible backfills, revenue realization reduces by 10% relative to spot due to churn/overhead.
- Conversion from GPU-hour economics to per-inference token UR: use average throughput 10k tokens/GPU-hour (synthetic, workload-dependent).

Key assumption block formulas (textual):
- Billable_backfill_hours = Offpeak_hours * Backfill_capture_rate
- Net_backfill_revenue = Billable_backfill_hours * Backfill_unit_revenue * (1 - Preemptible_discount)
- Effective_reserved_unit_cost = (Commit_cost - Net_backfill_revenue + Safety_buffer_costs) / (Total_billed_gpu_hours)

2) Hourly Utilization (tab):
- Table sample columns: Date | Hour | Reserved GPUs active | Estimated customer workload GPUs | Spare GPUs | Backfill sold GPUs | Revenue_this_hour
- Example row: 2026-02-14 | 02:00 | 120 | 18 | 102 | 40 | $18.00
- Notes: Spare GPUs = max(0, Reserved - Estimated_customer); Backfill sold <= Spare * capture_rate_cap; capture_rate_cap derived from orchestration limits and prep time.

3) Backfill Rules (tab):
- Rule A (safest): only use GPUs with idle time >= 90m contiguous; keep 12% headroom reserved for sudden peak bursts; preemptible backfills only; alert SRE on >3 preemptions/hr.
- Rule B (opportunistic): allow 30m idle window, headroom 6%, prefer non-preemptible for >2 hour blocks; revenue share with customers for live-testing partners.
- Rule C (aggressive): allow 0m minimum idle if model rollout flagged low risk; headroom 0% (no safety buffer), requires strict rapid-evict orchestration and hot-cache warmers.
- Each rule has an associated operational overhead multiplier (ops_hours_per_1000h): A=0.3, B=0.6, C=1.4 -> convert to $/GPU-hour ops cost assuming $150/hr average oncall/ops loaded.

4) Price Sensitivity (tab):
- Sweep variables: backfill_capture_rate [10%,20%,40%,60%,80%], backfill_unit_revenue [$0.20, $0.35, $0.45, $0.65], safety_buffer [0%,6%,12%].
- Output metric: delta effective unit cost relative to baseline (no backfill). Also compute commit_runway_improvement = reduction in required committed GPUs to hit same effective unit cost.
- Example cells (text):
  - Baseline per GPU-hour effective cost = Commit_cost / (Reserved * hours_in_month) = $432,000 / (120 * 24 * 30) = ~$0.50/hr
  - With 40% capture @ $0.45 revenue, net revenue = Offpeak_hours*0.4*0.45 -> translates to effective cost reduction to ~$0.37/hr (illustrative).

5) Scenario Summary (tab):
- Conservative: 20% capture, $0.35 revenue, 12% safety -> Effective cost = $0.46/hr, monthly saving vs baseline = $8,100, commit runway improvement = ~3 GPUs equivalent.
- Base: 40% capture, $0.45 revenue, 6% safety -> Effective cost = $0.37/hr, monthly saving = $24,300, commit runway improvement = ~12 GPUs equivalent.
- Optimistic: 70% capture, $0.65 revenue, 0% safety -> Effective cost = $0.29/hr, monthly saving = $57,600, commit runway improvement = ~28 GPUs equivalent.
- Add a stress case that includes 15% preemptions and 7% extra ops cost -> show sensitivity effect on net.

6) Key Outputs & Actions (tab):
- Key charts to add: heatmap of hour-of-week spare capacity, waterfall of cost reduction (gross revenue -> net revenue -> ops cost -> net savings), commit reduction curve by target effective cost.
- Recommended short experiments (first 90 days):
  1) Pilot region: one data center (EU-west) enable Rule A backfills for low-risk customers; target capture 25%-30% offpeak within 30 days.
  2) Instrumenting metrics: add "eviction rate", "backfill fulfillment latency", "customer cold-start errors" to Console per-route dashboard.
  3) Billing UX: show guaranteed vs monetizable hours on contract UI (so sales can sell a blended product).
- Action items (owners):
  - Priya D: run integration test with billing team for revenue attribution (due 2026-03-15).
  - Rafael O: build 7-day heatmap widget in Console (due 2026-03-01).
  - Marcus L: prototype orchestration policy for Rule B (POC infra branch) (due 2026-03-22).

Open questions / risks:
- Customer acceptance: even small SLA regressions may blow out churn; need careful canarying.
- Legal/compliance: selling backfill to third parties may have data locality implications; route for Private customers must be disabled.
- Accounting: how to credit backfill revenue against committed cost in ARR/TCV calculations.

Notes to reviewer:
- This sheet intentionally converts GPU-hour economics to per-token numbers only for rough sense-making; do not use in contract language.
- Where possible, replace synthetic token throughput with per-customer measured throughput when running pilots.
- Next revision will include hourly-level simulated traces (Monte Carlo) to capture variance in capture_rate and eviction churn.

Bottom-line (working statement): If we can safely monetize a modest fraction of off-peak slack (~30–40%) with low operational overhead, we can reduce the effective committed unit cost by ~20–30%, which translates into non-trivial reductions in committed footprint or the ability to lower customer price points while preserving margin. This sheet is a rollout-ready workbook to quantify trade-offs and communicate with Sales/Finance on blended contract constructs.
